rejected.title: The trial balance
card: A trial balance is a list of every ledger account and its balance, taken at one date. Debit balances go in one column and credit balances in the other.
Each column is added up. If every transaction was recorded with equal debits and credits, the two totals are the same.
If the totals differ, there is an error to find. Examples are a debit posted with no matching credit, or an amount copied wrongly into one account.

Equal totals do not prove the books are right. An error can leave debits and credits equal, such as a transaction left out completely, or a debit and credit made to the wrong accounts for the right amount.
rejected.remember: A trial balance checks that debits equal credits, but it cannot show that every entry is correct.

a.q: A trial balance has total debits of $84 500 and total credits of $84 500. What can the accountant conclude?
opts: Debits equal credits, but some errors may remain
Every account in the ledger has the correct balance
No transaction has been left out of the ledger
Each entry was posted to the correct account
a.why: Equal totals show only that debits and credits balance. Errors such as a missing transaction or a wrong account can still be present, so the other options claim too much.
a.clue: Equal totals test one thing only.

b.q: Priya's Pet Supplies pays $300 for electricity. The bookkeeper debits Rent Expense $300 and credits Cash at Bank $300. What will the trial balance show?
opts: Equal totals, so the error is not detected
Debits higher than credits by $300
Credits higher than debits by $300
Debits higher than credits by $600
b.why: The debit and credit were both $300, so the totals still agree. The debit went to the wrong expense account, and a trial balance cannot detect that. A $300 difference would need an error such as a debit posted with no matching credit.
b.clue: Were the debit and credit amounts equal?
